newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil state to pick power selloff adviser.
newsitem.headline: Brazil state to pick power selloff adviser.

text.p: The Brazilian state of Rio Grande do Sul plans to take bids on March 4 to choose a consultant to advise on the break-up and partial selloff of its energy sector, state officials said.
A spokeswoman for Rio Grande do Sul said the winning consultant will be named in late March and will have until late June to complete its work.
"At the end of July, the state will publish bid specifications with sale dates and base prices," she said.

In December 1996, the state said it intended to split state power firm Companhia Estadual de Energia Eletrica (CEEE) into six firms which will be controlled by a holding company. State coal miner Companhia Riograndense de Mineracao (CRM), which produces 35 percent of all the coal in Brazil, will be split into two companies.

"The (adviser) will be responible for elaborating a sale model for shares of the new (power) distributors to be privatized and for common shares of the new CEEE, which will remain under state control," the statement said.
Assis de Souza, Rio Grande do Sul's energy, mines and communications secretary, said the naming of an adviser is yet another step toward the state's goal of improving infrastructure.
In December, the state sold off a strategic 35-percent voting stake in its telecom Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes (CRT) for 681 million reais.
"The process of opening the capital of CRT is concluded and now it is the electrical energy sector's turn," Souza was quoted as saying.
The spokeswoman called the state's restructuring and partial spinoff of energy assets "an immense project" far exceeding the CRT shares sale.
The state plans call for CEEE to be broken into three power distributors, two generators and one transmission firm.

Two distributors are to be privatized. A power generator valued at 700 million reais will be handed to the federal government in lieu of state debts and three others will remain majority state-owned but be opened to private capital.
Meanwhile, CRM's coal mining unit will be privatized while its exploration and concession arm will remain state-owned.
